papers.title: Action Learning for Scientific Simulations
papers.summary: Understanding and controlling how systems evolve is central to science and engineering, where many problems require reasoning about complete trajectories. Existing approaches typically learn local dynamics or generate trajectories, but objectives constructed from individual transitions can miss dependencies across time, while generative models do not necessarily provide a tractable objective for evaluating and optimizing arbitrary paths. We study $\textit{action learning}$, the problem of recovering a stochastic action from trajectory observations, yielding a common objective for reasoning about dynamical systems. We introduce $\textbf{LEAP}$ ($\textbf{L}$earned $\textbf{E}$nergy on $\textbf{A}$ction $\textbf{P}$aths), which anchors the unknown action to a tractable reference process and learns the remaining correction by comparing observed trajectories with reference trajectories. This construction yields a differentiable objective on path space that can capture both local dynamical structure and nonadditive dependencies across time. Once learned, the same action can be flexibly reused for path ranking and inference, mechanism steering, constrained optimization and sampling. Across stochastic physical systems, many-body orbital dynamics and molecular simulations, LEAP recovers underlying dynamics, captures dependencies across time and enables transfer across inference objectives and physical conditions. We show that $\textit{action learning}$ is a promising framework for turning trajectory observations into reusable objectives for scientific inference and control.
papers.title_ja: 科学シミュレーションのためのアクションラーニング

papers.title: Consensus-Based Distributed Filtering for Angles-Only Tracking in Cislunar Space
papers.summary: This paper investigates consensus-based distributed filtering strategies for multi-observer angles-only navigation in the cislunar space. The objective is to estimate the inertial state of a target spacecraft using only line-of-sight measurements collected by a network of observer spacecraft. This problem is particularly relevant for autonomous cislunar navigation, where ground support may be limited, and centralized fusion architectures may be problematic due to communication and computational constraints, and single-point failure risks. Three distributed filtering approaches are considered: the Distributed Extended Kalman Filter, the Information-Weighted Consensus Filter, and the Kalman Consensus Filter. All methods share the same local prediction and measurement-processing steps, but differ in the way information is exchanged and fused across the network. Their performance is evaluated and compared to a centralized Extended Kalman Filter, adopted as benchmark, and independent local filters in a high-fidelity cislunar scenario. Numerical simulations show that the distributed approaches significantly improve estimation accuracy with respect to independent filters. Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses are then conducted to characterize the robustness of the considered methods to finite consensus iterations and prior misalignment among the agents.
papers.title_ja: シスルナ空間における角度のみ追跡のためのコンセンサスベース分散フィルタリング

papers.title: Decentralized Bi-Level Optimization for Cooperative Orbital Transportation of a Rigid Payload
papers.summary: The rapid growth of the space economy, alongside increasing orbital congestion and debris, is driving demand for reliable on-orbit transportation of large and non-cooperative objects. Performing such transportation with a swarm of small spacecraft distributes risk and removes the single point of failure inherent to monolithic architectures, but requires solving a non-convex trajectory optimization coupling every agent's cone-constrained thrust to the payload's rotational dynamics. Existing approaches span decentralized control laws with asymptotic guarantees but limited constraint enforcement, and centralized and partially centralized planners that reintroduce a single point of failure. In this work, we present a decentralized bi-level framework driven by exact gradients: the problem is split into an inner convex thrust allocation and an outer search over payload torque trajectories. This decomposition yields fuel-efficient solutions quickly, without requiring full NLP convergence, and at short timescales its performance scales with the number of agents. Theoretical convergence guarantees are established, and the method is validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulation, including closed-loop recovery from in-flight faults. These properties make the framework well suited to spacecraft swarm applications.
papers.title_ja: 剛体ペイロードの協調軌道輸送のための分散型二層最適化

papers.title: Accelerating Wildfire Hazard Mapping Across Canada with an AI Surrogate Modelling Framework
papers.summary: Canada's increasing wildfire activity requires frequent national hazard mapping to guide proactive mitigation, including fuel management, land-use planning, infrastructure protection, and evacuation routing. However, process-based wildfire simulation frameworks (e.g., BurnP3 and BurnP3+) rely on computationally intensive Monte Carlo simulations to model burn probability, fire intensity, and rate of spread. These workflows can take days to weeks to process a single regional modelling unit. To overcome these computational bottlenecks, we present three contributions developed through collaboration between AI researchers and wildfire modelling experts: (a) a standardized framework for training, fine-tuning, and evaluating AI surrogate models against process-based wildfire simulators; (b) a multi-task deep learning surrogate trained on national-scale data to emulate burn probability, mean fire intensity, and mean rate of spread at a fraction of the computational cost (seconds); and (c) domain-specific metrics and counterfactual evaluation protocols to probe out-of-distribution generalization. Integrating geospatial data (fuel, terrain, ignition likelihood) and regional weather, our model approximates BurnP3+ simulation outputs, achieving strong performance across agreement, rank-correlation, error, and spatial-overlap metrics. It preserves downstream hazard classifications and produces physically plausible responses to expert-informed counterfactual interventions. On a representative region, the surrogate achieves 806-fold end-to-end CPU acceleration and uses 13% of BurnP3+'s host memory, facilitating rapid scenario analysis.
papers.title_ja: AIサロゲートモデリングフレームワークによるカナダ全域の山火事危険度マッピングの高速化

papers.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
papers.summary: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.
papers.title_ja: 変化する初期/最終条件におけるリアルタイム多エージェント経路計画のためのTransformerベースのアプローチ

papers.title: RheOPT: Few-Shot Non-Newtonian Flow Prediction via Newtonian Pretraining of RheOFormer
papers.summary: Despite advances in numerical methods, non-Newtonian flow simulations remain computationally expensive because velocity and stress must be advanced together through rate- and history-dependent constitutive dynamics. Neural-operator surrogates reduce inference cost after training, but their training data require the same expensive simulations they aim to replace, making data-efficient learning essential when only a few non-Newtonian simulations can be afforded. Here, we introduce the Rheological Operator Pretrained Transformer (RheOPT), which pretrains a transformer-based neural operator on inexpensive Newtonian simulations and fine-tunes it on a small number of non-Newtonian samples. Rather than transferring the Newtonian constitutive response itself, RheOPT reuses geometry-conditioned transport structure that remains useful after the stress model changes. We evaluate RheOPT in two geometry-matched settings: a $4{:}1$ contraction channel for Giesekus, Oldroyd-B, and Bingham fluids, and the oscillatory wake behind a triangular obstacle for Oldroyd-B flow. In the contraction, Newtonian pretraining substantially improves few-shot prediction, and a model fine-tuned on four target samples can match or exceed a from-scratch model trained on four times as many. This benefit is reliable under reversible instance normalization (RevIN) but dataset dependent under Global normalization, a difference we trace to the dynamic range of each fluid's velocity and stress fields. In the wake, where relative $L_2$ error alone cannot verify that vortex shedding is recovered, phase-insensitive diagnostics show that pretraining recovers the shedding frequency and wake fluctuation amplitude that are suppressed by the from-scratch model in the few-shot regime. Overall, RheOPT establishes Newtonian simulation as a physically grounded pretraining source for data-efficient non-Newtonian operator learning.
papers.title_ja: RheOPT: ニュートン流体事前学習による非ニュートン流体の少サンプル流動予測
papers.summary_ja: 非ニュートン流体のシミュレーションコストを削減するため、安価なニュートン流体データでトランスフォーマー型ニューラルオペレータを事前学習し、少量の非ニュートン流体データでファインチューニングする手法RheOPTを提案する。幾何学条件付きの輸送構造を再利用することで、4サンプルでのファインチューニングが4倍のデータ量でゼロから学習したモデルと同等以上の性能を発揮することを示した。さらに、相対L2誤差では検出しにくい渦放出の周波数や振幅も、事前学習により少サンプル環境で正しく復元できることを診断指標で検証した。

papers.title: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
papers.summary: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive. Generative models provide continuous latent representations, but their latent spaces can have thousands to tens of thousands of dimensions, creating a regime where the latent dimension $D$ greatly exceeds the evaluation budget. We introduce SABLE, a Bayesian optimisation method for high-dimensional latent spaces with an isotropic distribution and limited budget. SABLE uses a Bayesian affine surrogate for prediction and acquisition, treating higher-order structure as surrogate discrepancy. After $N$ observations, the slope update has dimension at most $N-1$, yielding a decomposition of each query into an in-span component optimised by expected improvement (EI) in at most $N$ dimensions and an off-span component governed by a scalar norm. We show that the off-span norm implicitly selected by affine EI can lead to underexploration, and SABLE instead prescribes it using a finite-horizon schedule, without restricting search to a learned subspace. A recompression scheme reduces information to $\mathcal O(M)$ pseudo-observations, bounding refitting cost by $\mathcal O(M^2D+M^3)$ while keeping parameter inference, prediction, and acquisition decisions to tens of milliseconds. Across synthetic benchmarks and latent-space optimisation tasks, SABLE achieves high sample efficiency and reduces decision time by several orders of magnitude at large budgets.
papers.title_ja: SABLE: スケーラブルなアフィンベイズ潜在空間探索
papers.summary_ja: 高次元な生成モデルの潜在空間において、評価コストが高い条件下で効率的な最適化を行うためのベイズ最適化手法SABLEを提案する。同手法はアフィンサロゲートモデルを用い、観測数Nに依存する低次元成分とスカラーノルムで制御される高次元成分にクエリを分解することで、探索と開発のバランスを最適化する。再圧縮スキームにより計算コストを大幅に削減し、大規模予算下でも決定時間を数桁短縮しつつ高いサンプル効率を実現した。

papers.title: Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow
papers.summary: We build structure-preserving reduced-order models for both challenge problems of the AePW-4 High-Speed Working Group. They are a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 (RC-19) and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85 (HyMAX). The published data for each case hold no time-resolved response and no repeated runs. The physics must therefore be carried by the form of the model. One construction gives two models per problem. A Ritz-Galerkin reference model describes the plate. A learned model keeps the reference model's exact potential, fits the remaining generalized forces, and trains only a dissipation that cannot add energy. Its energy balance holds for any weights by construction. On the trained model the worst relative residual is 2.2e-15. On RC-19, shock relations predict a pressure ratio of 1.521 across the panel. Pressure-sensitive paint measured the same value. Thirty runs of the learned model place the mean dominant frequency within 1.0% of the measured 236 Hz. At one periodic and one chaotic condition, the learned model reproduces the response regime of a published reduced-order model in all sixteen runs. It does so without that model's 113 Hz spectral peak, which the measurements do not show. Measured displacements can also correct the chaotic response through one more force that respects the energy balance. We tested this on synthetic data at the experiment's 5 kHz sampling rate. The state error is 1.25% of the panel thickness without noise and 3.5% with 10 micrometers of noise. On HyMAX the learned model follows the reference model's trailing-edge displacement for 65 ms with a relative error of 3.7%. These results show that a model whose structure carries the physics can match measured flutter behavior when the available data cannot train it.
papers.title_ja: 超音速・高マッハ数流場における薄板の構造保存型縮約モデル
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、超音速および高マッハ数流場における薄板の振動特性を捉える構造保存型縮約モデル（ROM）を構築する。Ritz-Galerkin法による参照モデルのポテンシャルエネルギーを厳密に保持し、残りの一般化力とエネルギーを増加させない減衰項のみを学習する手法を採用している。このアプローチにより、データが限定的な条件下でも物理法則（エネルギー収支）がモデル構造に組み込まれ、測定値と一致する精度で乱流やカオス的な応答を再現できることを示した。

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Dimension Reduction and Surrogates for Partially Linear Bayesian Inverse Problems
papers.summary: Many Bayesian inverse problems are characterized by two parameter vectors with distinct roles. A medium property, operator coefficient, or geometry block enters the forward model nonlinearly, whereas a volumetric, initial condition, or boundary condition source enters linearly. General-purpose nonlinear surrogates must relearn this known source dependence from data and may not preserve the correct source scaling outside the training regime. We introduce a structure-preserving partially linear (SPPL) framework that constructs separate reduced spaces for outputs, (linearly appearing) sources, and (nonlinearly appearing) medium variables and represents the reduced forward map as an affine function of the retained source coordinates, with coefficients that depend on the medium variables. Here, "affine" refers to the retained, mean-centered source coordinates: the physical forward map remains linear in the source, while the affine offset is induced by the source-prior mean and vanishes when that mean is zero. The analysis first identifies the optimal blockwise ridge approximation and then derives the optimal affine-in-source approximation under independent medium and source priors. A direct decomposition of the forward error into output, source, medium, and surrogate contributions yields blockwise spectral criteria and prior-predictive expected-KL control. For a Gaussian source prior, the optimal affine-in-source approximation coincides with the optimal blockwise ridge approximation. In a coseismic numerical example, a three-model controlled ablation on common block-reduced coordinates separates the effects of coefficient-matrix supervision and structure-preserving affine-in-source parameterization. Reduced-space surrogate MCMC provides orders-of-magnitude online acceleration relative to high-fidelity posterior sampling.
papers.title_ja: 部分線形ベイズ逆問題における構造保持次元削減とサロゲート
papers.summary_ja: ベイズ逆問題において、線形と非線形で現れるパラメータを区別し、既知の線形構造を保持するサロゲートモデルを構築する手法を提案する。出力・ソース・媒質変数それぞれに対して独立した縮約空間を定義し、ソース座標に対するアフィン関数として前進写像を表現することで、訓練範囲外でも正しいソーススケーリングを維持する。ガウスソース事前分布の下では、このアフィン近似が最適なブロックワイズリッジ近似と一致することを理論的に示す。同震動の数値例において、高忠実度後方サンプリングに対して桁違いのオンライン高速化を実現し、構造保持が精度と効率の両面で有効であることを実証した。

papers.title: CARS: a centerline-anchored attention surrogate for coronary blood flow on skeleton-generated lumen geometries
papers.summary: When the parameter of a PDE surrogate is the flow domain itself, the key/value set of an attention model must encode that domain. We present CARS (Coronary Artery Rapid Surrogate), a learned surrogate for the finite-volume solution map of the steady incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on coronary lumens built from image-derived centerlines. CARS maps a centerline with per-point lumen radius and a scalar inlet flow rate to pressure and velocity at arbitrary query points. The attention focal set is the case's own centerline, so geometry fusion costs $O(N n_f)$ rather than $O(N^2)$ in the number of evaluation points. Trained per territory on $2{,}700$ OpenFOAM solutions with synthetic focal lesions, CARS reaches relative $\ell_2$ errors of $0.120/0.149$ (pressure/velocity) on left-coronary and $0.063/0.119$ on right-coronary test sets, in $87$~ms per case against a solver wall-clock of $572$-$1{,}063$~s. It outperforms four parameter-matched neural operators, and accuracy saturates eightfold below the operating focal count. Fractional flow reserve derived from the predicted pressure matches the CFD label at Pearson $r = 0.941/0.993$ and reproduces the $\mathrm{FFR}\le 0.8$ decision in $97.7\%/96.3\%$ of held-out cases. The predicted velocity does not satisfy continuity closely enough for derived quantities, and the weights are territory-specific.
papers.title_ja: CARS: 骨格生成された冠動脈管腔幾何学における血流のための中心線アンカー型アテンションサロゲート
papers.summary_ja: 画像由来の中心線から構築された冠動脈管腔における定常不可圧Navier-Stokes方程式の数値解を、アテンション機構を用いたサロゲートモデルで高速推定する手法を提案する。幾何情報をキー/バリューセットとしてエンコードすることで、評価点の数に対する計算コストをO(N^2)からO(N n_f)に低減し、CFD求解器の数百秒に対し87msで圧力と速度を予測する。4つのパラメータ一致したニューラルオペレータを上回る精度を示し、FFR（血流予備能）の判定精度も高いが、速度の連続性満足度が低く、領域特異的な重み付けが必要という限界もある。

papers.title: MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models scale model capacity efficiently by activating a small subset of parameters per token. However, in long-context inference, memory remains a major bottleneck because the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length. Existing KV cache compression methods reduce this cost for dense transformers, but overlook a problem specific to MoE: KV eviction can change which experts are selected during answer generation, degrading the generation quality. We propose MoEZip, a routing-aware KV cache compression for sparse MoE language models. To estimate the sensitivity of expert routing to perturbation, we propose a novel metric based on the Fisher information matrix of routing distributions. MoEZip combines this metric with attention weights for routing-aware scoring of contexts. Finally, we compose a complementary scoring system that combines eviction methods for dense and sparse-MoE architectures. Experiments show that MoEZip achieves robust performance under aggressive cache compression on various benchmarks. At a KV retention ratio of 10\%, MoEZip improves over the SoTA baseline by +24 and +20 points on average on LongBench and RULER, corresponding to 2.3$\times$ and 4.9$\times$ higher scores, respectively.
papers.title_ja: MoEZip: スパースMixture-of-Experts LLM向けのルーティング認識型KVキャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary_ja: MoE言語モデルにおける長文脈推論時のメモリボトルネックを解決するため、KVキャッシュ圧縮手法MoEZipを提案する。既存手法が見過ごしていた、KVの破棄によるエキスパート選択の変化（ルーティングドリフト）を、ルーティング分布のフィッシャー情報行列に基づく指標で定量化する。この指標とアテンション重みを組み合わせたルーティング認識型スコアリングにより、生成品質の劣化を抑えつつキャッシュを圧縮する。実験では、KV保持率10%の条件下でLongBenchおよびRULERにおいて既存最良手法を大幅に上回る性能を示した。

papers.title: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz
papers.summary: Muon updates matrix-valued parameters along approximately orthogonalized directions and often trains large language models faster than AdamW, yet it remains unclear when and why orthogonalization helps. We study PolarGD, the orthogonalized update at the core of Muon, on matrix quadratics, where optimizers can be analyzed in closed form, and compare update directions under line search to remove the effect of learning-rate tuning. Orthogonalization pays off when the gradient is far from low rank and its largest singular directions see high curvature. PolarGD reaches the minimizer in one step whenever the rows of the error are orthogonal with equal norms, for any Hessian, whereas gradient descent needs all Hessian eigenvalues to be equal; and unlike sign descent, PolarGD is unaffected by rotations of the problem. Over many steps, PolarGD acts as gradient descent preconditioned by the current iterate, so its speed is governed by the conditioning of the iterate rather than of the Hessian. This explains fast regimes as well as a slow one, caused by tiny singular values of the iterate, in which PolarGD is much slower than gradient descent. Finally, the few Newton-Schulz iterations used in Muon treat these tiny singular values as gradient descent does, so fewer iterations can converge faster than exact orthogonalization; in a transformer trained with Muon, about a quarter of the singular values of the attention matrices fall in this regime.

papers.title: Route-and-Generate: KL-Regularized Router Improvement for Reasoning Routing in LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models often apply complex reasoning indiscriminately, leading to overthinking on simple tasks and underthinking on harder ones. We present Route-and-Generate (Rouge), a hierarchical training framework that enables LLMs to adaptively decide when and how much reasoning is required for each input. Our approach decouples reasoning effort allocation from answer generation by introducing a routing policy that allocates a fixed sampling budget across multiple reasoning formats, while the base model is optimized with GRPO using per-sample rewards. To promote efficient reasoning, we employ a rank-based reward that favors shorter correct solutions, and update the routing policy via a closed-form KL-regularized policy improvement step distilled into a neural router. This design encourages concise answers on easy problems while reserving longer reasoning for harder ones, achieving improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across multiple reasoning benchmarks.
papers.title_ja: Route-and-Generate: LLMにおける推論ルーティングのためのKL正則化ルーター改善
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）が単純なタスクで過剰に推論し、難しいタスクで推論不足になる問題を解決するため、推論努力の配分と回答生成を分離する階層的学習フレームワーク「Route-and-Generate」を提案する。ルーティングポリシーにより複数の推論形式にサンプリング予算を割り当て、ベースモデルはサンプルごとの報酬を用いたGRPOで最適化する。より短い正解を優先するランクベース報酬と、KL正則化されたポリシー改善ステップによりニューラルルーターを蒸留し、効率性と精度のトレードオフを改善する。

papers.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.

papers.title: Same Beliefs, Different Policies: Learning Reusable Representations for Early Stopping in LLM Reasoning
papers.summary: Reasoning LLMs often continue reasoning after reaching a correct answer, wasting computation and sometimes replacing it with an incorrect one. Deciding when to stop is a metareasoning problem: the model must weigh what further reasoning could achieve against its cost, given what it can already answer. Direct utility training learns a stopping representation at a chosen token price; supporting new prices can require additional controller training. We introduce BELT (BELief-based Termination), which separates outcome prediction from stopping control. It learns beliefs about current and future answers from a frozen LLM's hidden states, then fits a linear stopping policy on the frozen features. The prediction targets are independent of token price, so one probe supports different accuracy-cost trade-offs through CPU policy refitting or threshold adjustment. Averaged over five out-of-distribution (OOD) math benchmarks, BELT reduces generated tokens by 41% on Qwen3-1.7B and 51% on OLMo-3-7B-Think without loss of accuracy. The same math-trained BELT transfers to coding and agentic tasks without training on code or agentic data. In all three domains, its accuracy-cost trade-offs are competitive with or better than those of end-to-end controllers. On OLMo3, its probe has 21.2x fewer parameters than one checkpoint of the strongest baseline, OS-Pruner, and needs 55x fewer training GPU-hours than OS-Pruner's five price-specific checkpoints.

papers.title: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures
papers.summary: Recent work in additive manufacturing and neural inverse design enables the creation of complex three-dimensional structures to manipulate physical fields, yet these designs must also adhere to discrete, non-differentiable fabrication constraints. Current methods limit the design space by imposing differentiable soft manufacturability loss penalties, or by fixing structures through post-processing, causing a discrepancy between the geometry optimized by the physics model and the final fabricated result. Thus, we present AcoustiPrint, a physics-informed neural architecture for constrained inverse design that represents three-dimensional geometries with an implicit neural representation (INR) and passes each candidate through a printability operator before evaluating its final response. The printability operator executes layer-wise self-support, discrete material selection, and whole-body connectivity, assuring fabrication feasibility. To allow for backpropagation through the discrete non-differentiable operations, we use surrogate gradients for the backward pass and a self-supervised printability objective that progressively drives the INR toward a valid design domain. We demonstrate AcoustiPrint for personalized transcranial focused ultrasound, where inter-patient differences in acoustic properties and head geometry deform wave propagation and requires patient-specific acoustic focusing. AcoustiPrint jointly optimizes three-dimensional geometry and material composition through differentiable wave physics while ensuring manufacturability. Experiments show manufacturable acoustic structures with enhanced focal accuracy and over density-based and phase-based baselines, demonstrating a generalized methodology for neural design through non-differentiable manufacturing constraints and differentiable physics.
papers.title_ja: AcoustiPrint: 製造可能な音響構造の物理ガイド型ニューラルデザイン

papers.title: PhysibleMDM: Enforcing Inference-Time Physical Feasibility Constraints on Motion Diffusion Models via Noise Optimization
papers.summary: Motion Diffusion Models (MDMs) can generate diverse and visually appealing human motion; yet, the resulting trajectories frequently violate physical constraints, limiting their downstream use in simulation and control. We present PhysibleMDM, a framework that promotes physical feasibility of MDM output by optimizing at inference time the diffusion noise without retraining the generative model. We introduce a set of surrogate feasibility constraints that can be evaluated without full trajectory simulation. These constraints combine kinematic checks (e.g., ground penetration, slip, and self-collision) with dynamic feasibility tests computed via an inverse-dynamics inner loop formulated as a cone program. We solve the resulting black-box noise optimization problem using the Separable Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (Sep-CMA-ES), thereby avoiding reliance on computationally expensive and discontinuous gradients. An autoregressive scheme then chains optimized segments to synthesize long motion sequences. Across 100 motion styles on an SMPL humanoid, PhysibleMDM reduces mean ground penetration, self-collision penetration, and ground slip by 75%, 92%, and 74%, respectively, relative to unoptimized diffusion output. Across 11 sequences for a custom bipedal robot, it achieves median reductions of 89.5% in per-sequence mean acceleration-reconstruction error and 79.5% in the mean inverse-dynamics residual.

papers.title: QuaNAS: Uncertainty-Aware Reuse of Earlier Searches for Query-Efficient Neural Architecture Search
papers.summary: Neural architecture search (NAS) on a new dataset often affords only tens of short training runs, so what the search knows before its first evaluation decides its efficiency. Yet most NAS methods start from scratch, guided at best by zero-cost proxies that are unreliable across tasks. QuaNAS treats a library of earlier searches in the same search space as explicit knowledge of uncertain reliability. Main effects of design decisions learned from this library and, secondarily, zero-cost proxies become priors over candidate architectures without any label of the new dataset. A Gaussian process starts at the prior optimum and re-estimates after every evaluation how far each prior is trusted. Under a protocol frozen before any confirmation data were seen, QuaNAS was evaluated once on 12 new image, time-series, text and tabular datasets. It lowered anytime regret on the short-training objective 2.7- to 3.9-fold relative to five pre-specified NAS baselines that start from scratch (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0012 each). Its final models matched (non-inferiority margin 0.5 pp) or exceeded matched-recipe reference models on nine datasets, as did the prior optimum, selected without a single evaluation. Post-hoc comparisons with established transfer methods given the same library trace the gain to the library: without it, the same Gaussian process had over twice the regret. They also show where each transfer mechanism works best: the pooled main effects of QuaNAS for weakly transferable tabular tasks, per-task surrogates for image, time-series and text tasks and for small or mismatched libraries. Finally, the main effects make the transferred knowledge inspectable.

papers.title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
papers.summary: Automated agentic-system design is typically evaluated on static task suites with immediate scalar rewards. Deployed systems face persistent shift, delayed dependent feedback, correlated component failures, and costly architecture changes. We formalize meta-agent architecture search as sequential incumbent replacement with switching costs and hard risk constraints and introduce Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS). CMAS retrieves archived architectures and proposes typed graph edits, then scores each against the incumbent by paired shadow replay under common random numbers, with interventional component credit. Promotion requires an empirically calibrated, variance-penalized simultaneous score above a pre-specified margin, and is followed by a simulated canary stage and pre-specified rollback. Since backtests cannot certify meta-level skill, we introduce MetaInvest-Bench, a regime-switching simulator whose specified worker competence makes a surrogate-optimal architecture computable, with leakage-controlled replay, adversarial governance tracks, and five negative controls. Financial streams serve as a risk-sensitive testbed for meta-level generalization; we claim no alpha. Across 96 streams, CMAS cuts normalized mean surrogate dynamic-oracle regret from 0.116 to 0.104 and raises held-out utility from 0.44 to 0.48 over the strongest adaptive baseline; when extra workers add no value, it contracts to near-single-agent teams. Its deployment inference cost is ~6% lower, though its search-inclusive token cost is the highest of the methods compared. The observed per-update false-promotion rate is 3.4% against a nominal 5% target, and 4.8% in a sealed rerun. The calibration is empirical: it concerns an update-level replay statistic on an author-designed benchmark, and guarantees neither full-utility improvement, nor absence of simulated canary-stage harm, nor sequence-level error control.

papers.title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
papers.summary: We developed a machine learning (ML) surrogate trained on instantaneous large eddy simulation (LES) data filtered using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) to predict mean flow fields in natural rivers with complex geometries. The surrogate enables efficient prediction of mean flow fields downstream of marine hydrokinetic (MHK) turbine arrays at a fraction of the computational cost of high fidelity simulations, facilitating turbine layout optimization in natural waterways where bathymetry, turbulence, and turbine interactions influence the available energy resource. We demonstrate the capabilities of the model at a real world tidal river site under ebb tide conditions. Complex bed bathymetry and planform geometry generate substantial background turbulence that can obscure turbine wake signatures. POD is employed to extract relevant flow structures, improving the ability of the ML model to learn wake dynamics. First, LES is performed at the tidal site to generate training data. POD is then applied to decompose the instantaneous LES fields into spatial modes. Selected modes are used to train a three dimensional convolutional encoder decoder network to predict time averaged velocity fields. This selective filtering reduces the influence of dominant background fluctuations while preserving information relevant to turbine wakes. At equivalent network size and training cost, the POD filtered surrogate reduces the mean squared error by three orders of magnitude compared with the same network trained on unfiltered LES data.

papers.title: Low-Latency MoE Inference in Space Data Centers: A Wireless-Power-Transfer Perspective
papers.summary: Space data centers (SpaceDCs) are emerging as platforms for large language models (LLMs), supported by continuous solar-energy harvesting and high-speed interconnections. The mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture supports distributed LLM inference by deploying experts across satellites. However, skewed expert activation creates uneven computation power demands despite uniform solar-power supply at the dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit (SSO). Consequently, active experts remain power-constrained while harvested power at idle experts is underused. These reduce inference efficiency and increase latency. To address this supply-demand mismatch, we propose the SpaceWPT framework, which uses inter-satellite laser-based wireless power transfer (WPT) to redistribute harvested power. The key design challenge is to balance the computation demands of power-donating and power-receiving satellites under WPT losses: transferring more power accelerates computation at the receiver but leaves less power for the donor. After deriving design principles that simplify WPT control, we characterize the resulting latency tradeoff through a tractable surrogate of average inference latency. Minimizing the surrogate yields a novel two-sided water-filling strategy that determines whether each active expert donates, retains, or receives power according to the water level and its WPT link efficiency. Simulations with Mixtral-8x7B and Phi-3.5-MoE show up to 29.25% lower inference latency than without WPT, with larger gains under more compact formations and higher transfer efficiencies.
papers.title_ja: 宇宙データセンターにおける低レイテンシMoE推論：無線電力伝送の視点から
