papers.title: CTRL-FM: Inference-Time Structural Control for Flow-Based Virtual Sensing under Long-Horizon Node Outages
papers.summary: Long-horizon node outages are harder than conventional missing-value imputation because complete sensor trajectories remain unobserved for extended periods, while the usefulness of spatial and temporal dependencies varies across outage locations and operating regimes. Existing graph, diffusion, and flow-based methods typically impose a fixed structural bias, which can oversmooth abrupt changes or propagate errors from unreliable neighbors. We introduce CTRL-FM, an observation-preserving flow-matching framework that treats structural guidance as an outage-conditioned inference-time decision. A missing-only flow-matching backbone learns a conditional velocity field while keeping observed measurements exactly fixed. For each realized outage, CTRL-FM constructs self-supervised proxy outages from surviving measurements and uses their known values to select among uncontrolled, graph-dominant, temporal-dominant, and balanced control policies. The selected policy is locally modulated by graph and temporal reliability estimated exclusively from surviving observations, while boundary-anchored trends provide structural guidance. Control is applied only to missing entries and is rejected when proxy evidence does not sufficiently improve over uncontrolled sampling. Across PeMS08, METR-LA, Air-36, and AQI, CTRL-FM achieves the strongest overall performance under 30% and 60% node outages. Stress tests with up to 75% sensor loss further show graceful degradation and consistent gains over training-time and fixed structural control. These results demonstrate that validating, selecting, and locally adapting structural guidance for each realized outage is more effective than imposing a single global structural prior.
papers.title_ja: CTRL-FM: 長時間ノード停止時のフローベース仮想センシングにおける推論時構造制御
papers.summary_ja: センサーの長時間欠損に対し、固定された構造バイアスではなく、推論時に動的に制御ポリシーを選択するフローマッチングフレームワークを提案する。生存している観測データから自己教師ありでプロキシ欠損を生成し、グラフ依存・時間依存・バランス型の制御戦略を適応的に選択・調整する。観測値を厳密に固定しつつ欠損部分のみを補完し、証拠が不十分な場合は制御を拒否する仕組みにより、PeMS08などの実データセットで既存手法を上回る性能と頑健性を示した。

papers.title: Soft Ontology Priors over Latent Concept Posteriors for Weakly Supervised Neuro-Symbolic Learning
papers.summary: Neuro-symbolic (NeSy) predictors that supervise only the task label suffer from reasoning shortcuts: distinct concept mappings achieve the same maximum likelihood, leaving the recovered concepts unidentifiable and unsafe for downstream reuse. We attack this failure by injecting a soft ontology prior over the latent concepts into the training objective and compiling it together with the task constraint into a smooth, decomposable probabilistic circuit. Under independent Bernoulli perception, the normalisers of the resulting structured concept posterior reduce to weighted model counts that are linear in the compiled circuit size, because the neural leaf weights fold into the circuit before evaluation. The soft compilation strategy places expert axioms in the circuit's weights rather than its support (task-structural axioms guaranteed by the data-generating process stay hard), so noisy expert axioms only redistribute prior mass and cannot empty the support. We characterise how the prior reweights label-restricted shortcut mass through differences in ontology violation energy, show that soft priors incur bounded log-density perturbations under bounded axiom noise, and prove that the hard-support counterpart can be made degenerate by a single corrupted axiom. We validate these predictions on an audited six-concept view of the real-world BDD-OIA driving benchmark and on controlled NeSy tasks.
papers.title_ja: 弱教師ありニューロシンボリック学習における潜在概念事後分布へのソフトオントロジー事前分布
papers.summary_ja: ニューロシンボリック学習において、タスクラベルのみで学習した場合に生じる推論の近道（ショートカット）問題と概念の識別不能性を解決する手法を提案する。潜在概念に対してソフトなオントロジー事前分布を導入し、これを確率回路としてコンパイルすることで、正規化定数を効率的に計算可能にする。このアプローチにより、ノイジーな専門家公理がモデルのサポートを空にするリスクを回避しつつ、事前分布による重み付けを通じて推論の安全性と再利用性を向上させる。BDD-OIAドライビングベンチマークおよび制御されたNeSyタスクで、理論的予測と実証結果の一致を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 深層学習と論理推論の融合手法であり、ML手法全般に関心があるため中程度に関連。

papers.title: MIG-COW: Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Deepfake Detectors via Gradient Decomposition
papers.summary: Despite recent advances, deepfake detectors remain vulnerable to adversarial examples, particularly in diverse, real-world settings. We propose MIG-COW, a novel adversarial attack framework that generates highly generalizable and visually imperceptible adversarial examples. By combining momentum-integrated gradients with a consensus-orthogonal decomposition, MIG-COW captures both shared and model-specific vulnerabilities across heterogeneous CNN and ViT detectors. On the AADD-2025 Challenge benchmarks, MIG-COW achieves a 99.96% white-box attack success rate (ASR) with high perceptual similarity (SSIM), significantly outperforming existing baselines. However, its limited 7.16% ASR against official black-box targets - despite achieving the best overall score - highlights the ongoing challenge of transferability. We also demonstrate that incorporating low-performing but diverse models in the ensemble can degrade attack effectiveness, underscoring the need for careful surrogate model selection in real-world adversarial settings.
papers.title_ja: MIG-COW: グラデーション分解によるディープフェイク検出器への転移可能な敵対的攻撃
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ディープフェイク検出器に対する転移可能な敵対的攻撃フレームワーク「MIG-COW」を提案する。モーメンタム統合勾配とコンセンサス直交分解を組み合わせ、CNNとViTの異種検出器間で共有される脆弱性とモデル固有の脆弱性を同時に捉える手法である。AADD-2025チャレンジのベンチマークにおいて、白箱攻撃では99.96%の高い成功率と高い視覚的類似性を達成し、既存手法を上回った。一方で、黒箱ターゲットに対する成功率は7.16%と低く、転移性の限界を示すとともに、アンサンブルにおけるサロゲートモデル選定の重要性を指摘している。

papers.title: Prediction Is Not Calibration: Item Parameter Recovery and Representation Coupling in Knowledge Tracing
papers.summary: Knowledge tracing (KT) models can estimate item parameters through an item response decoder trained solely for next-response prediction, yet predictive accuracy does not guarantee parameter recovery. We study 2PL, GPCM, and NRM decoders paired with LSTM, Transformer, and DKVMN encoders. Response-model derivatives show why discrimination and option slope updates depend directly on the scale and spread of estimated ability. Affine logit identities show how item-dependent shifts and rescaling in estimated ability are absorbed into item parameters without changing response probabilities. In simulations, difficulty, mean threshold, and correct-option intercept recovery remain high under shuffled order across representation widths, whereas discrimination and keyed option slope contrast recovery require wider item representations and degrade further under fixed item order. Separating the sequence item representation (width $d_S$) from the item parameter key (width $d_M$), and pairing a wide key with a thin sequence representation ($\mathrm{SK}(64,8)$), reduces fixed-order ability distortions and improves recovery and cross-order consistency without sacrificing test accuracy or increasing model size relative to a shared width-64 baseline ($\mathrm{SH}(64)$). On TIMSS and EdNet, widening $d_M$ consistently improves agreement with an offline IRT reference, while the trade-off from narrowing $d_S$ depends on the encoder's reliance on sequence width for prediction. These findings show why item parameters, especially discrimination and option slopes, must be evaluated separately from response prediction.
papers.title_ja: 予測はキャリブレーションではない：知識トレースにおける項目パラメータの復元と表現結合
papers.summary_ja: 知識トレースモデルにおいて、次応答の予測精度が高いことと項目パラメータ（識別力や選択肢の傾きなど）の正確な復元は一致しないことを示した。LSTMやTransformerなどのエンコーダとIRT系デコーダの組み合わせを分析し、能力推定のスケールや分散が項目パラメータに吸収されるメカニズムを理論的に解明した。シミュレーションでは、項目表現の幅を拡大することで固定順序下での復元精度が向上し、シーケンス表現と項目キーの幅を分離することで、モデルサイズを増やさずに一貫性を高めることが確認された。TIMSSやEdNetなどの実データでも、項目表現の拡大がオフラインIRT基準との一致度を改善することが実証された。

papers.title: GANet: A Lightweight Group Attention Network for Plant Disease Identification on Embedded Systems
papers.summary: Global warming and climate change are major catalysts for plant diseases, significantly affecting food production worldwide. Addressing this issue requires continuous monitoring and early detection of plant diseases. While recent advancements in deep learning offer potential solutions, most models demand high processing power and struggle to perform efficiently on low-end electronic hardware. Furthermore, many existing works focus on specific crop diseases, limiting their broader applicability. This paper presents a lightweight Group Equivariance Attention Network (GANet) designed for the prediction and monitoring of 38 types of plant diseases. GANet introduces a novel Group Attention block and Group-Wise Feature Fusion block, making it both sparse and efficient. With only 0.001M parameters, the model achieves an impressive 99.99% accuracy on the PlantVillage dataset. Additionally, GANet is optimized for deployment on edge devices such as the Raspberry Pi 4b and Jetson Nano, where it reaches 5 FPS and 11 FPS, respectively, demonstrating its potential for real-time plant disease monitoring on low-power devices.
papers.title_ja: GANet: 組み込みシステム向け植物病害識別のための軽量グループアテンションネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、低消費電力デバイス上で動作する軽量な植物病害識別モデル「GANet」を提案する。グループ等変性アテンションブロックとグループワイズ特徴融合ブロックを導入し、パラメータ数を0.001Mに抑えつつPlantVillageデータセットで99.99%の精度を実現した。Raspberry Pi 4bやJetson Nanoなどのエッジデバイス上で5〜11 FPSの処理速度を達成し、リアルタイム監視の適用可能性を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMや軌道力学とは無関係だが、モデルの軽量化・推論高速化という技術的関心に一部該当する。

papers.title: Half-Slot Link Scheduling for Open GNSS with $x$-Tx $y$-Rx Multibeam Phased Array Antennas
papers.summary: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSSs) are evolving from closed navigation constellations toward open space infrastructure capable of serving extensive spacecraft users. This evolution requires the constellation to support navigation ranging, telemetry (TM) return, and telecommand (TC) delivery for users while preserving its own ranging and communication functions.Existing phased-array payloads onboard BeiDou satellites provide one transmit (Tx) beam and one receive (Rx) beam. Such a configuration was designed mainly for intra-constellation operation, and can become a resource bottleneck when a large number of users share the same link opportunities. Upgrading GNSS satellites to phased-array terminals with $x$-Tx and $y$-Rx beams is therefore a natural enhancement. This paper develops a staged dynamic half-slot link scheduling framework (SDHSS) for open GNSS with $x$-Tx $y$-Rx multibeam phased-array antennas. The framework models navigation, TM, and TC as three different services, reserves the essential ranging and ground-access opportunities required by the GNSS constellation, and then allocates the remaining half-slot beam resources according to current service demand. To support multibeam concurrency, feasible links are selected through dynamic service-layer ordering and beam-copy matching. Simulations based on a BeiDou constellation show that the proposed method protects GNSS baseline operation and provides stronger external navigation, TM, and TC performance than fair contact planning. The results further show that additional Tx and Rx beams can be effectively converted into multi-service capability. This work establishes a link-scheduling approach for extending GNSS from constellation-internal operation to large-scale spacecraft service support.
papers.title_ja: オープンGNSSにおけるx送信y受信マルチビームフェーズドアレイアンテナのための半スロットリンクスケジューリング
papers.summary_ja: オープンGNSSが多数の宇宙機ユーザーにサービスを提供する際、既存の単一ビーム構成ではリソース不足が生じる問題に対し、x送信・y受信ビームを持つフェーズドアレイアンテナ向けの動的半スロットリンクスケジューリングフレームワーク（SDHSS）を提案する。本手法は、GNSS自体の測位・通信機能を確保しつつ、残りのビームリソースを現在のサービス需要に基づいて動的に割り当てることで、測位、テレメトリ、テレコマンドの3種サービスを並行処理する。北斗衛星コンステレーションを用いたシミュレーションにより、公平な接触計画よりも優れた外部サービス性能を示し、追加ビームを効果的にマルチサービス能力に変換できることを実証した。

papers.title: Do Machine Learning-Guided Proactive Full Capacity Protocols Mitigate Emergency Department Overcrowding? A Simulation-Based Evaluation
papers.summary: Objective: Emergency department (ED) overcrowding threatens care quality, yet Full Capacity Protocols (FCPs) are typically activated only after crowding thresholds have been exceeded. This study evaluated whether machine learning-guided proactive FCP activation improves ED crowding control compared with conventional reactive activation. Materials and Methods: We developed and validated an integrated machine learning and discrete-event simulation framework representing ED patient flow and capacity management. An embedded machine learning model predicted hourly waiting-room crowding six hours ahead and triggered proactive FCP activation. Using empirically calibrated operational parameters from a large US hospital, we compared proactive and reactive deployment strategies over a 365-day simulation horizon with 10 independent replications. Outcomes included ED length of stay, wait time, percentage of time above the crowding threshold, number of FCP activations, and protocol duration. Results: Proactive deployment produced statistically significant reductions in the percentage of time above the crowding threshold and average protocol duration across all threshold settings. It also reduced crowding variability and extreme congestion events, resulting in smoother ED operations. Although proactive deployment generally improved ED length of stay and wait time, these differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion: Embedding machine learning predictions within an operational simulation enables proactive, prediction-guided capacity management before severe congestion develops. These findings support the feasibility and potential value of proactive FCP deployment as a decision-support strategy for improving ED crowding control and provide evidence to support prospective implementation in clinical practice.

papers.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
papers.summary: We study $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel.We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. papers.title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
papers.summary: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) models are often shared without their training data, assuming this protects the patients who contributed them. However, a model can reveal whether a patient's records were used in training, a privacy breach known as a membership inference attack. This risk is usually reported as a cohort average, which can appear negligible while individual patients are almost certainly exposed. Identifying potentially vulnerable records before developing a production model could make privacy assessment more practical. We measured each patient's vulnerability to membership inference attack, across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets in four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models. Training choices changed how many patients had high attack scores, but the patients who ranked highest by risk largely stayed the same across the configurations we tested. Stronger weight decay reduced the exposed cohort up to threefold, yet largely the same patients remained most at risk across training recipes, architectures and initializations, including foundation models. Therefore, we developed a lightweight screening tool that uses four small models to identify patients with high risk of exposure before production-model training. We also assessed if flagged patients could be protected without removing their data. Privacy screening should become incorporated into data preparation for clinical AI.

papers.title: New criteria for upper bounds on the number of limit cycles in Li\'enard systems
papers.summary: We study upper bounds for isolated periodic orbits of generalized Li\'enard systems on a single potential well. Common-curvature and common-intercept conditions yield uniqueness and hyperbolicity, while a convex--concave condition on the potential-profile slopes gives an upper bound of two. The statements allow finite unequal potential endpoints; appropriate versions also admit degenerate restoring forces and reduced regularity. We prove a uniqueness extension across slope interfaces, a quantitative joint weak-damping criterion, and a compensation criterion controlled by two derivatives. A separate response comparison at neutral cycles, combined with a connected parameter-family argument, gives a coefficient criterion for a two-cycle bound. Applications include classical quartic systems, negative-parameter and positive-parameter Selkov systems, a uniqueness conjecture for arbitrary-degree polynomial systems, and explicit smooth and nonsmooth examples. Existence is proved separately whenever an exact count is asserted. Restrictions to a potential well, a parameter region, or a compact width interval are retained throughout.

papers.title: First Results of Calculation of the Dayside Magnetopause Reconnection Rate with TRACERS
papers.summary: Quantifying the rate of reconnection remains a key challenge in the study of geomagnetic storms. In this study, we present the first results from the new Tandem Reconnection and Cusp Electrodynamics Reconnaissance Satellites (TRACERS) mission to calculate the reconnection rate from dispersed ion populations measured in the cusp, using previously developed methodology. We study ion dispersion events in two storms. During the first storm, which occurred on September 30, 2025, 21 dispersion events were identified in TRACERS 2 ion data as a combined result of geospace dynamics and the spacecraft cusp encounters. Throughout this time when ion dispersion was detected by TRACERS , the reconnection rate is calculated and is shown to track reasonably well with another measure of geomagnetic activity, the Cross Polar Cap Potential (CPCP) as obtained by the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN). The dispersions are correlated with the smoothed CPCP, and a correlation of $r^2=0.62$ was found using the dispersions from the onset and main phase of the storm. The correlation disappears when including dispersions from the recovery period. The distribution of reconnection rates throughout this storm lies generally between 0.1 - 1.5 mV/m, slightly lower than previous reconnection rates calculated with DMSP, but consistent with in-situ observations made with Polar. In this work, we also apply a previously developed automatic identification algorithm for ion-energy cusp dispersion to TRACERS, with the intent that it may serve as a tool for future statistical analysis as the data volume becomes too large to manually review.
